summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:requesting-code-review, sent the reviewer template to a subagent through the Agent tool, and correctly flagged both seeded defects (the pagination offset and the unawaited saveOrder) as Critical. It did not approve the diff. The run still fails on precision: Important finding #9 calls the module-load readFileSync of config.json in src/config.js a defect, and the story lists that code as correct. Separately, Important #10 (package.json) gives a file but no line number.
reasoning: Criteria 1–4 pass. Criterion 7 fails: the reviewer filed "src/config.js:7-9 — config loading is an unrelated change with no error handling or validation… It is also less safe than what it replaced" under Important (Should Fix). The main agent repeated it in its summary under the Important heading. A blocking finding about code the story says is correct is exactly what criteria 5–11 rule out. Criterion 12 is also unclear-to-failing, because Important #10 cites package.json with no line number. The other "correct code" items were praised or got only Minor findings.

observations.description: Precision miss: the reviewer filed the intentional startup readFileSync of config.json (src/config.js:7-9, commented 'Read once at startup') as Important #9, recommending try/catch and schema validation. That is a blocking finding against code this story defines as correct.

The reviewer filed 8 Important findings, several of them speculative or product questions (duplicate IDs flagged as 'ambiguous', no hasMore, no npm test script). Calling these 'Should Fix' dilutes the two real Critical defects. The main agent itself said several are 'genuinely underspecified... rather than outright defects' but did not move them down to Minor.

The main agent's summary condensed the subagent's Important findings (renumbered, file/line kept but trigger detail dropped). It mentioned that a 'Codex review gate' exists but held it until after a fix pass; this is extra skill machinery the user didn't ask for.
On the onboarding screens, the default selection for both the folder-trust and bypass-permissions prompts is 'No, exit', so pressing Enter by reflex quits the app.

While dispatching, the main agent said 'It's running in the background — I'll report its findings when it reports back'. It did report back without being prompted, which is good. It also independently re-read handlers.js and store.js to verify both Criticals.

criteria.criterion: Invoked requesting-code-review skill and dispatched a reviewer subagent with the Agent tool
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review"}}, then Read of code-reviewer.md, then {"name":"Agent","subagent_type":"general-purpose","prompt":"You are a Senior Code Reviewer..."}. The subagent log is subagents/agent-acd93bad3374d05e4.jsonl.

criteria.criterion: Flags the listOrdersHandler pagination offset as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent output, under Critical: "1. src/handlers.js:18 — off-by-one offset makes the first page of orders unreachable... {page:1, size:10} returned ord_00000010 … ord_00000019"

criteria.criterion: Flags the unawaited store.saveOrder in createOrderHandler as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent output, under Critical: "2. src/handlers.js:37 — store.saveOrder is async and is neither awaited nor caught; a bad order returns 201 and crashes the process", with a reproduction showing "rows in store: 0"

criteria.criterion: Review does not approve the diff
criteria.evidence: Subagent: "Ready to merge? No." Main agent: "Verdict: not ready to merge."

criteria.criterion: No Critical/Important finding asserts a defect in the listed correct code (umbrella for 6–11)
criteria.evidence: Fails because of item 7: Important #9 targets the config.js readFileSync (see criterion 7).

criteria.criterion: withRetry not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: withRetry is praised in Strengths ("correctly written for what it is"). The only findings about it are Minor #11 (attempts<1) and Minor #12 (retry wraps the read path).

criteria.criterion: Module-load readFileSync of config.json not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: Under 'Important (Should Fix)': "9. src/config.js:7-9 — config loading is an unrelated change with no error handling or validation... less safe than what it replaced: a missing or malformed config.json now throws a bare ENOENT/SyntaxError at require time... wrap the read in a try/catch". The main agent's summary keeps this under Important.

criteria.criterion: parseOrderId not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: Strengths: "parseOrderId is a proper parse-don't-validate helper (src/util.js:21-25)". No finding about it.

criteria.criterion: listOrders returning orders.slice not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: Strengths: "orders.slice(offset, offset + limit) (src/store.js:6) returns a copy — a real safety improvement"

criteria.criterion: catch in listOrdersHandler that logs and rethrows not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: None of findings #1–14 in the subagent output targets the catch/log/rethrow. Logging is mentioned only in Minor #11 ("list failed: undefined").

criteria.criterion: Fixed clock and seeded 25-order list in tests not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: Strengths praises seed() as "realistic fixture data including a deliberate partial final page". Important #3 and #4 are about the weak assertions and the missing success-path test, not the fixtures. The shared-state point is Minor #14.

criteria.criterion: Every Critical/Important finding cites file:line plus a trigger and its outcome
criteria.evidence: Most findings meet this (e.g. #1 handlers.js:18, #2 handlers.js:37, #5 handlers.js:16-17 'size=-5 → 0 rows'). Important #10 cites only "package.json — there is no test script, so npm test fails", with no line number. Important #8 (handlers.js:24, no hasMore) describes a missing feature more than an input-to-outcome defect.
